The proposed hemispherical-disk calculation supplies the missing sign directly for either sign of p and q, including absolute value one, without changing the theorem.

required_own_edits.source_excerpt: Its abelianization under $x\mapsto q$, $y\mapsto p$ is $cq-dp=-1$, so it is opposite the positive normal-disk meridian, whose class is the positive generator by [F3].
required_own_edits.proposed_replacement: To calibrate signs geometrically, the positively oriented coordinate cores representing $x$ and $y$ bound the hemispherical disks $D_x=\{\operatorname{Im}z_2=0,\ \operatorname{Re}z_2\ge0\}\cap S^3$ and $D_y=\{\operatorname{Im}z_1=0,\ \operatorname{Re}z_1\ge0\}\cap S^3$, oriented by their respective core boundaries. The knot meets $D_x$ transversely in $|q|$ points, each with intersection sign $\operatorname{sgn}(q)$, and meets $D_y$ in $|p|$ points, each with sign $\operatorname{sgn}(p)$. For the first sign, at a point where $z_2$ is positive real, the ambient orientation is the complex $z_1$ orientation followed by increasing $\operatorname{Im}z_2$; the component of the knot tangent transverse to $D_x$ has sign $q$. For the second, at positive real $z_1$, the ambient orientation is increasing $\operatorname{Im}z_1$ followed by the complex $z_2$ orientation, and the transverse tangent component has sign $p$. Deleting small disks about these intersections gives oriented surfaces in the knot complement with boundary relations $[x]=q[\mu]$ and $[y]=p[\mu]$, where $\mu$ is the positive normal-disk meridian. Thus the abelianization $x\mapsto q$, $y\mapsto p$ sends this geometric meridian to $1$: [F3] makes $[\mu]$ a generator, and the displayed relations and $\gcd(p,q)=1$ fix its sign. The disk-boundary curve $m$ has abelianization $cq-dp=-1$, so its orientation is opposite to that positive meridian.
